title: Adaptive prefetch budgeter and memcpy coalescer to cut host overhead
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Background: Host-side prefill and decode pipelines currently spend disproportionate CPU cycles on small scatter-gather memcpy operations and threadpool context switches. This increases p99 latency and prevents close-to-linear scaling when concurrency rises. Objective: Implement an adaptive prefetch budgeter that dynamically throttles host prefetch depth per GPU queue using real-time kernel probe feedback and per-stream pinned buffer availability. In parallel, implement a memcpy coalescer that merges small host->device copies into larger DMA-friendly operations with alignment and lifetimes heuristics tied to KV cache residency. Integrate both changes with the kernel-selection hinting layer so we avoid extra copies when a chosen kernel supports zero-copy or direct-mapped tensors.
Deliverables: 1) Budgeter module with metrics and config knobs (min/max depth, probe smoothing). 2) Coalescer library with lock-free queue and alignment strategies. 3) New dedicated copy threadpool that is NUMA-aware and cooperatively parked to reduce interference. 4) E2E tests, microbench harnesses, and canary rollout plan. Success criteria: - Reduce average host CPU time per request by >= 30% for common 512-token workloads. - Reduce p99 prefill latency by >= 25% under 100 concurrent streams. - No regressions in throughput for long sequences (>2048 tokens).
acceptance_criteria: Unit and integration tests for budgeter and coalescer pass in CI
Bench harness shows >=30% CPU reduction on sample workload (512 tokens)
p99 prefill latency decreases by >=25% in staged load tests
No correctness regressions (output tokens identical within allowed nondeterminism)
Canary rollout in us-west shows stable tail latencies for 72h
notes: 2025-02-11: Spike shows small memcpy ops (<4KB) account for ~42% of host memcpy time on prefill path.
2025-02-14: Prototype coalescer reduces memcpy syscalls by ~65% in microbench; need alignment fixes for pinned buffers.
2025-02-18: Chose lock-free SPSC queues per stream to avoid global contention; fallback to MPSC for shared copy pool.
2025-02-21: Kernel-selection hook added to avoid coalescing when kernel supports direct-mapped input buffers.
